With vaccinations progressing and policy support in place, the FOMC’s July 28, 2021 decision to keep the federal funds rate at 0–0.25% and continue Treasury and agency MBS purchases remains appropriate for sustaining the recovery and anchoring inflation expectations under average-inflation targeting. The July 2021 SLOOS corroborates an improving credit backdrop: banks reported stronger C&I loan demand across large, middle-market, and small firms; higher borrower inquiries; and easing terms on C&I loans. On the household side, banks eased standards for consumer loans (including credit cards and autos) and reported stronger demand for qualified mortgages, while CRE standards eased for multifamily. Foreign banks also reported stronger C&I demand. Reasons cited for easing—improved economic outlook, competition, greater risk tolerance, and ample liquidity/capital—signal broader credit availability and support the transmission of accommodative monetary policy.

Balancing these positives with the Financial Stability Report’s cautions—elevated valuations, high business leverage, nonbank funding vulnerabilities, and sectoral risks in CRE (office and lodging)—the outlook remains supportive but measured. On net, SLOOS evidence tilts sentiment modestly more positive than before.
